perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab ships AAMP 2.3 with human approval thresholds on ad spend
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab released AAMP 2.3, a spec that requires human approval gates before AI agents can commit ad budgets above set thresholds. This is a concrete governance standard for agentic ad buying — the kind of rule that shapes how platforms are built and how buyers must configure automated systems going forward.

stories.head: AI speeds marketing production, but measurement still lags behind
stories.plain: Teams are using AI to produce content faster, but most still track clicks rather than business outcomes. This means AI's real ROI is invisible to budget holders, creating a structural gap between what AI can do and what marketers can prove — a problem that will drive demand for better attribution and measurement tooling.

stories.head: AI-generated web content is widening digital accessibility gaps
stories.plain: Generative AI is producing more of the web, but it consistently reproduces accessibility failures — missing alt text, poor contrast, broken screen-reader flows. Marketers who own digital experience now face legal and reputational risk if they ship AI-generated content without accessibility checks baked into their governance workflows.

stories.head: AI buyer simulations fall short without personality data
stories.plain: Synthetic audiences built from behavioural signals alone produce skewed predictions because they omit personality traits that drive purchase decisions. The article argues that richer psychographic inputs are the next frontier for AI-powered audience modelling — which has direct implications for how CDPs and personalization engines should be fed.

stories.head: Blotato API lets AI agents read and reply to Instagram DMs and comments
stories.plain: Blotato added inbound messaging endpoints so a single API key lets an AI agent both publish posts and respond to DMs and comments autonomously. This closes the loop on social engagement automation, making it easier to deploy agentic systems that manage real customer conversations at scale without human handoffs.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab ships AAMP 2.3 with human approval thresholds for AI ad agents
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab's updated Autonomous Advertising Marketplace Protocol adds governance rails — including human-approval spending thresholds, privacy controls, and platform integrations — so AI agents can buy and manage ads in production without going rogue. This is a standards-level move that affects every ad-tech vendor and media buyer building agentic systems.

stories.head: How to measure marketing when AI owns the discovery layer
stories.plain: When AI answers replace search results, clicks and impressions stop reflecting real demand. This piece lays out how to rebuild analytics — tracking brand mentions in AI responses, engagement signals, and buyer intent — so marketers can prove value in a world where the funnel starts inside a chatbot.

stories.head: Yelp plugs its reviews and local business data directly into ChatGPT
stories.plain: Yelp's review corpus and business listings are now a live data source inside ChatGPT, giving OpenAI richer local context and giving Yelp prime placement inside AI-generated answers. For local and multi-location brands, this reshapes where reputation management and lead generation actually happen.

stories.head: Stop buying 'AI' — buy specific capabilities instead
stories.plain: Greg Kihlström argues that the label 'AI-powered' now means nothing in vendor pitches — buyers should demand capability-level specifics (what decision does it make? what data does it use?) before signing. Practical procurement guidance that changes how marketing leaders evaluate and compare tools.

stories.head: AI buyer simulations miss personality — limiting synthetic audience accuracy
stories.plain: Synthetic audiences built from behavioral and demographic signals consistently mis-predict decisions because they omit personality traits. The article explains which psychological dimensions matter most and what data teams need to add to make AI-simulated buyers genuinely useful for campaign planning and personalization.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Job of Marketer
body: The dominant shift this month is not AI assisting marketers — it is AI executing tasks end-to-end, from answering Instagram DMs to managing Google Business Profiles to running ERP workflows. The marketer's role is migrating from doer to director, which requires a completely different skill set than most teams currently have.

IAB Tech Lab's move to standardise AI agents for real advertising, and the proliferation of autonomous agent platforms (Unanet's Champ, Blotato's DM responder), signals that infrastructure is catching up to the vision. Organisations that don't define governance for agent behaviour now will find themselves correcting it at scale later.
ev: MarTech · IAB Tech Lab & ad agents

themes.head: Measurement Breaks When AI Owns Discovery
body: As AI intermediaries (ChatGPT, Yelp-in-ChatGPT, search generative experiences) become the first point of contact between brands and buyers, traditional attribution models collapse. Clicks and sessions no longer represent the full customer journey — a finding underscored by Prime Day data showing 9 % more clicks but 45 % less consumer spending, a gap that standard dashboards cannot explain.

The measurement crisis is compounding: production speed has accelerated thanks to AI, but the ability to prove what worked has not kept pace. Until teams invest in new measurement frameworks — cross-channel, AI-aware, and outcome-focused — faster content creation simply generates more unaccountable spend.
ev: MarTech · Production speed vs. measurement lag
MarTech Series · Prime Day click/spend gap

themes.head: The Race to Build AI-Proof Differentiation
body: Multiple pieces this month converge on a single anxiety: if AI can replicate content, simulate buyers, and automate campaigns, what is left that competitors cannot instantly clone? The answer emerging is proprietary data, genuine brand personality, and human relationships — the exact assets that AI buyer-simulation tools admittedly miss.

Trust is being positioned as the new moat. Articles on making trust a competitive differentiator, closing the gap between brand promise and sales reality, and stopping the reflex to 'buy AI' rather than buy capabilities all point to the same strategic conclusion: durable advantage lives in what AI cannot synthesise — context, credibility, and community.

themes.head: AI Tooling Expands Reach While Creating Accessibility Debt
body: AI-generated digital experiences are being deployed faster than accessibility standards can follow. Auto-generated layouts, dynamic content, and AI-written copy routinely fail screen readers, contrast requirements, and keyboard navigation — meaning speed gains for the majority create exclusion for millions of users with disabilities.

This is not just an ethical issue; it is a legal and reputational liability that is growing in proportion to how much of the web AI now builds. Organisations need to add accessibility audits to every AI content pipeline, not treat them as a post-launch checklist item.
ev: MarTech · 4 questions before AI in event workflow
Agile Brand · Stop buying AI, buy capabilities

themes.head: Creator & Local Channels Become Scalable Programmatic Inventory
body: Two previously 'high-touch' channels — YouTube creator sponsorships and Google Business Profiles — are being systematically automated and made buyable at scale. Agentio's platform turns individual creator deals into a programmatic growth engine, while MyAds.Guru applies AI management to local business listings. The boundary between performance media and relationship-based media is dissolving.

Simultaneously, email is reasserting itself as a high-ROI channel (with budget shift data to back it), and Yelp's integration into ChatGPT is turning local reviews into AI-served leads. The common thread is that trusted, intent-rich inventory is being re-packaged for algorithmic buying — which raises fresh questions about brand safety and authentic voice at scale.
ev: MarTech Series · Email ROI budget shifts

month.takeaway: Across every story this month, the underlying pressure is the same: AI is accelerating execution faster than organisations can build the measurement, governance, and human-centred strategy needed to direct it — meaning the teams that invest in those foundations now will compound an advantage that pure tooling adoption cannot buy.
